links.comparator_used: Same AI-3 algorithm as validated off-the-shelf in the validation phase, before retraining on DR stages, DME grading and referral guidelines (compared across phases, not a concurrent arm)
links.outcome: Diabetic retinopathy detection sensitivity and specificity versus reference standard
links.effect: Sensitivity rose from 68.4% to 99.6%; specificity fell from 96% to 64.7%. After training, DME sensitivity was 26.5% and referable DR sensitivity was 78.9%.
links.tradeoff: Specificity dropped to 64.7%, which the authors partly attribute to cataracts and media opacity increasing false positives. DME sensitivity stayed low. Comparison is confounded by different settings, populations and graders between phases.
links.quote: The AI-3 algorithm’s sensitivity increased significantly from 68.4% to 99.6%, while specificity decreased from 96% to 64.7% between the validation and implementation phases.
